problem: On-policy RL for ObjectNav has been stuck with shallow GRU policies because deep or wide transformers are unstable and far too slow to train with RL. Imitation-learned transformer agents such as SPOC plateau near 57% success on CHORES-S. Scaling SPOC's expert data 23x (SPOC*, 2.3M trajectories) only reaches 60.0%, which the authors attribute to too little state-space exploration and error recovery in expert data.
motivation: RL explores by trial and error and can surpass shortest-path expert demonstrations, but it is sample-inefficient, and naive causal transformers cost O(t^2) per rollout step. The paper asks whether SPOC-style transformer architectures can be combined with massively scaled on-policy RL in procedurally generated houses. The goal is a sim-only RGB navigator that transfers to real robots without adaptation.
key_idea: Train a fully transformer-based policy with DD-PPO at large scale, made affordable by a KV-cached causal decoder, hundreds of parallel multi-node rollouts with growing batch sizes, and a sped-up AI2-THOR. The policy is a frozen DINOv2 encoder, a transformer state encoder, and a Llama-2-style causal decoder, trained across 10k–150k ProcTHOR houses.
insight:
The ablation in Table 2a shows every capacity increase helps, summing to +13.6 average SR on ProcTHOR-10k val / ArchitecTHOR:
- CLIP-RN50 → DINOv2 ViT-S: +5.2
- 3-layer transformer decoder instead of 3-layer GRU: +5.5
- 1 → 3 decoder layers: +4
- ViT-S → ViT-B: +3.2

A transformer state encoder alone, with a GRU decoder, gives little (73.6/59.8 vs 73.1/60.8). The temporal transformer decoder is where RL benefits from capacity. Caching matters for making RL affordable: in Fig. 5 KV-cache gives 2,300 SPS for LoCoBot vs 150 with no cache (Stretch: 950 vs 110). CHORES val SR is still rising at ~700M steps, whereas IL with 23x more data (SPOC*) gains only 3 points. Difficulty tiers (Table 4) show the text-goal vs GT-b-box gap grows from ~9 points on Easy to ~13.7 on Hard. The authors read this as recognition errors plus a residual exploration problem. The main failure mode is memory degradation after visiting more than 4 rooms.
method: Visual encoder: frozen DINOv2 ViT (ViT-B/14 in the final model) produces patch tokens (H/14 x W/14 x h), which are reshaped and projected to d=512. The encoder is kept frozen for sim-to-real transfer.

Goal encoder: a one-hot category embedding for LoCoBot (following EmbCLIP), or the last hidden state of FLAN-T5-small on the language goal for Stretch. An optional bounding-box goal embeds 5 values (x1, y1, x2, y2, area) via sinusoidal positional encoding, coordinate-type embeddings and an MLP (g_b in R^{5 x d}).
Transformer state encoder: a 3-layer non-causal encoder (512-d, 8 heads) over [STATE token, visual tokens, goal tokens]. The STATE token output is a goal-conditioned state vector s_t.

Causal transformer decoder: a 3-layer Llama-2-style decoder (512-d, 8 heads) over s_0..s_t that builds a belief b_t. An episodic block-lower-triangular attention mask prevents attending across episodes, and a KV-cache makes rollout cost linear in t. Linear actor and critic heads sit on top.

Scalable RL recipe:
  - DD-PPO on 4 nodes / 32 A6000 GPUs / 512 CPU cores, with 192 (Stretch) or 384 (LoCoBot) parallel rollouts; ~3.4x speedup, ~4.5 days of training.
  - Constant LR; batch size is grown by increasing rollout length T=32→64→128 every 10M steps (final 49,152 frames for LoCoBot).
  - Reward: -0.01 per step, +10 on success, plus a distance-reduction term given only when a new minimum distance is reached.

Environment throughput for Stretch: continuous motion is approximated by teleport-with-capsule-collision-check (~40% faster simulation). Objaverse assets are loaded in Msgpack instead of Pickle (scene load ~25s→~8s). Together these raise SPS from ~550 to ~950 on ProcTHOR-150k houses with ~40k Objaverse assets.

PoliFormer-BoxNav: a variant whose goal is given only as a bounding box, so it can be 'prompted' zero-shot by Detic or GPT-4o. This enables open-vocabulary ObjectNav, multi-target navigation (resetting the KV-cache after each Done), human following, object tracking, room navigation and instance-description navigation.

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 visual encoder, plus a 3-layer transformer state encoder and a 3-layer causal transformer decoder trained from scratch with on-policy RL (DD-PPO). Goal encoder: FLAN-T5-small for the Stretch language goal, one-hot for the LoCoBot category.
setting.model_size: 'Hundreds of millions' of parameters (Fig. 1); no exact count reported. Encoder/decoder: 3 layers each, 512-d, 8 heads.
setting.training_data: Pure RL in AI2-THOR simulation, no demonstrations. LoCoBot: ProcTHOR-10k training houses, 435M steps. Stretch RE-1: ProcTHOR-150k houses with ~40k Objaverse assets (ObjaTHOR), ~700M environment steps. About 4.5 days on 32 A6000 GPUs.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB only (no depth, GPS/compass or map). Goal is a text/category, optionally plus a 2D b-box (ground truth in sim, Detic in the real world).
setting.action_space: Discrete. LoCoBot: MoveAhead 0.2 m, RotateLeft/Right 30°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done. Stretch RE-1: MoveAhead/MoveBack 0.2 m, RotateLeft/Right 30°, RotateLeft/RightSmall 6°, Done.
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (ProcTHOR, ArchitecTHOR, AI2-iTHOR, CHORES-S with Objaverse assets)
setting.privileged: None for the main RGB+text model. The b-box variants in simulation use ground-truth bounding boxes of the target; real-world b-box variants use Detic instead.

numbers_note:
Benchmarks, splits and settings:
- Split labels for CHORES-S (Table 1a) and the Table 4 difficulty tiers are not stated explicitly. 'val' is inferred from Fig. 1 ('Success Rate (%) on CHORES (val)'), so treat it with care.
- CHORES-S uses SEL rather than SPL.
- CHORES-S results include test-time augmentation and stochastic action sampling (following SPOC); 16-run re-evaluation gives mSR 82.5 ± 1.897.
- All b-box rows in simulation use ground-truth boxes and are not comparable to RGB-only methods.
- The ProcTHOR-10k val protocol (1500 tasks / 150 scenes) follows EmbCodebook.

Figure-only results:
- The Fig. 1 scaling curve over ~700M steps is given only as a figure.
- Fig. 5 training SPS by cache strategy is a bar chart: Stretch 110/560/850/950 and LoCoBot 150/1,170/2,050/2,300 for No/Feature/State/KV-cache.

Other:
- Table 2a ablation rows other than the ViT-S full-transformer row are omitted here.
- Minor inconsistency: the text gives LR 2·10^-4 while Table 3 lists 0.002.
results: PoliFormer reaches 85.5% SR (61.2 SEL) on CHORES-S ObjectNav with Stretch RE-1, beating IL-trained SPOC (57.0) by 28.5 points and SPOC* trained on 2.3M trajectories (60.0). With LoCoBot it sets SoTA on ProcTHOR-10k val (82.4 SR / 58.5 SPL vs EmbCodebook 73.7), ArchitecTHOR (68.3 vs 58.3) and AI2-iTHOR (85.3 vs 78.4). In zero-shot sim-to-real it achieves 83.3% on Stretch (vs SPOC 50.0) and 80.0% on LoCoBot (vs Phone2Proc 66.7, which is finetuned in reconstructed test scenes). With Detic boxes it reaches 88.9% on Stretch.
limitations: Needs very large compute (32 A6000 GPUs, ~4.5 days, hundreds of millions of steps) and hand-crafted reward shaping; extending to new tasks such as manipulation requires new reward design.
Memory degrades on long trajectories: after visiting more than 4 rooms the agent tends to revisit already-explored rooms, since there is no explicit map.
RGB-only and discrete actions for fair comparison, with separate models per embodiment (no cross-embodiment policy). Simulation b-box results rely on ground-truth boxes.
